facts.fact: WHO Eswatini reports that in November 2024 two consultants from its Regional Office, working with the country office and the Ministry of Health's M&E team, set up DHIS2 for Eswatini, customised its reporting tools and trained the M&E team to customise data collection tools and to integrate it with the Client Management Information System and other databases.

WHO Eswatini places DHIS2 within the Ministry of Health's Strategic Health Information Department, run by its M&E unit, and says that at set-up in November 2024 its domain and URL were hosted on UNICEF servers and that the M&E unit still needed WHO technical support and IT equipment to make it fully functional.

WHO Eswatini cites the end-term review of the National Health Sector Strategic Plan 2019-2023 as finding substantial progress in automating health facility clinical systems through deployment of the Client Management Information System, with data gaps and system integration remaining a barrier; the newsletter gives no date for the finding, so its published date of December 2024 is used.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health, Strategic Health Information Department (M&E unit), set up with WHO; hosted on UNICEF servers
systems.tiers: national; dashboards monitor how often reporting is done at facility level
an HMIS officer is pictured verifying data in a clinic in Lubombo

note: DHIS2 classed hmis on its description as the health sector's indicator reporting mechanism with facility-level reporting dashboards; CMIS classed emr on its description as the health facility clinical system. The document does not say who keys DHIS2 data or how many facilities use either system; it gives 327 health facilities in the country (clinics, health centres and hospitals) as visited by the 2024 HHFA. A WHO consultant is quoted in November 2024 that no existing database could show performance by region, inkhundla or facility.
